stem: In the series 7, 12, 19, 28, 39, ?, what term follows 39?

per_option_rationale.rationale: Adds 9 to 39 (the same difference as 28 to 39 was 11 minus the step size, misread as 9), giving 48.
Correctly identifies differences 5,7,9,11 and expects 13, but adds 13 to 39 and slips to 50 instead of 52.
Consecutive differences are 5, 7, 9, 11 - an AP with common difference 2. Next difference = 13. Missing term = 39 + 13 = 52.
Adds 17 to 39 assuming differences increase by 3 each time (5, 8, 11, 14, 17), giving 56.

explanation: The differences between consecutive terms are 5, 7, 9, 11 - an arithmetic sequence increasing by 2 each time. The next difference is 11 + 2 = 13. So the missing term = 39 + 13 = 52.

explanation_sections.punchline: When the series itself is not AP or GP, check differences - here the differences form an AP with step 2.
explanation_sections.approach: Apply clues most-certain-first: differences = 12-7=5, 19-12=7, 28-19=9, 39-28=11. These increase by 2 each step. Next difference = 11+2 = 13. Answer = 39+13 = 52.
explanation_sections.lesson: A second-level AP (differences of differences are constant) generates a quadratic-looking series. Check differences of differences.
explanation_sections.timing: 35-45 seconds. The key decision is computing the second-level differences to confirm they are constant at +2.
